//: Open-mode OpenCode config, rendered per task by the agent-plane supervisor ({env:*} filled from the task env). Structure = capability tiers, NOT role-play: ONE primary (`lci-open`) owns every write + both terminal tools (propose_pr/abort); subagents are least-privilege READ-ONLY helpers for context isolation. The terminal path is primary-only on purpose — the gate-interlock and recorder plugins key off the primary's terminal call, so a subagent must never be able to reach it. Other modes get their own rendering.

permission.//: Global invariant for every agent in open mode: no direct web egress (defense-in-depth over the ADR-0088 network allowlist). edit/bash are decided per-agent below, not here — so this baseline is NOT a duplicate of the primary's block.

lci-open.description: Lightbridge open mode: reads the ticket, investigates (delegating read-heavy digs to @explore), edits and builds/tests in the sandbox, then proposes a PR via the mediated lightbridge_propose_pr tool. Never pushes, never merges. The only agent that may write or call a terminal tool.

explore.description: Read-only investigation & localization — customizes OpenCode's built-in `explore`. Use it to answer a focused codebase question (where does X live, how is this pattern implemented, who calls this symbol) via read/grep/glob + the Lightbridge retrieval tools (semantic + graph search). It burns its own context window and hands back a distilled answer with file:line evidence, keeping the primary lean. Cannot edit, run commands, fetch the web, or propose a PR.

tools.//: Deny the mediated write/terminal tools by name — the permission block above can only gate edit/bash/webfetch, so this map is what actually keeps propose_pr/abort off a subagent. Retrieval + read tools stay enabled (unlisted = allowed). Tool names carry the `lightbridge` MCP-server prefix; finalized when the control-plane MCP surface lands.
